post.caption: The best diamond color grade is D. The Gemological Institute of America introduced this scale in 1953, and its president, Richard Liddicoat, was the architect of the system. Older systems used letters like triple A and phrases like blue white, and the institute wanted a fresh start, with no link to older grades. So it began at D, a letter not tied to top quality. The scale has 23 letters, running from D to Z, and D to F are colorless while G to J are near colorless. Graders compare each diamond with master stones, table down, in controlled light. The D to Z scale measures how little color a diamond has.
